headlines.title: French unrest compounds debt crisis fears. Paris-listed stocks, bonds and the euro fall
headlines.summary: When the people riot AND the bond market riots at the same time, you've got a real problem on the tape. French OAT spreads blowing out hits European banks, the euro, and forces the ECB's hand — this is a contagion story that can spill into U.S. credit markets fast. Watch the long bond and financials like BNP, SocGen, and anything with heavy European sovereign exposure.

headlines.title: China's third-quarter economic growth quickens to 4.5% as exports surge, beating estimates
headlines.summary: China printing a beat on GDP is a bid under commodities, EM equities, and anything with Asia exposure — think copper, iron ore, and the whole materials complex. But the export-driven nature of the beat means domestic demand is still soft, so don't get too excited about consumer plays. This moves the FXI, commodity ETFs, and sets the tone for multinationals reporting this week.

headlines.title: Iran's Main Oil Terminals Remain Empty as US Blockade Bites
headlines.summary: A genuine supply squeeze story — Iranian barrels going dark for weeks is the kind of thing that keeps oil elevated and puts a floor under energy names. Pair this with the Egypt-Houthi escalation and Hormuz transit fears, and the whole Middle East risk premium is getting repriced in crude. Energy sector and defense names get a bid; airlines and refiners feel the squeeze.
